1.1.text:
Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Muna Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Muna Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Muna. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Muna Regency. 5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia, can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and includes persons who are legally recognized as Women. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child in the womb. 8. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 9. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life. 10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, serious injury or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death. 12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, sexual abuse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences physical suffering, psychological suffering, sexual suffering, either directly or indirectly resulting from acts of violence. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems they face. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence to family or community who can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs. 22. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their roles normally both in the family and in society. 23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Institution is an agency/service/department/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance. 25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, Safe House, Child Social Protection House, Trauma Center Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter, etc. 26. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and child victims of violence. 27. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and child victims of violence. 28. Safe House is a temporary residence provided to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 29. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion either directly or indirectly based on human differences on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group or class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs resulting from reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 30.

CHAPTER II

PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

Article 2

Protection of women and child victims of violence is carried out based on the principles of: a. respect for human rights; b. gender equality and justice; c. non-discriminatory; d. protection of victims' rights; e. legal certainty.

CHAPTER IX MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 25

1. To ensure synergy, continuity and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, the Regional Government conducts monitoring.
2. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence in the region.
3. Monitoring is conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Apparatus Organizations that implement policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence.
4. Monitoring is conducted from the planning stage up to the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence for the current year.

Article 30

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or Non-Governmental Organizations and Universities that implement protection for women and children victims of violence.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), is in accordance with the regional financial capacity and is implemented in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Article 8

The obligations of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 5 letters c and d who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as family members.

Article 8

The obligations of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 5 letters c and d who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as family members.

Part Two Principles and Service Standards

Article 19

1. Services to women and children victims of violence as referred to in Article 10 are carried out comprehensively and in an integrated manner across sectors, professions, and disciplines of knowledge.
2. Services as referred to in paragraph (1) are organized with the principles:a. non-discrimination;
b. equality:c. protection and confidentiality;
d. honesty:e. empowerment; andf. integration.
3. Services to women and children victims of violence are carried out based on service standards in accordance with laws and regulations.
4. Service mechanisms for women and children victims of violence are organized according to standard operating procedures.
5. Standard operating procedures as referred to in paragraph (4) are further regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER VIII COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 24

1. The community and business sector have the right to participate in the prevention of cases of violence against women and children, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence.
2. Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out individually or jointly, either by individuals or institutions.

CHAPTER VII INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS

Article 20

1. Services for women and children victims of violence as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (1) are carried out through an integrated service mechanism.
2. Integrated services as referred to in paragraph (1) are established at the regency, sub-district and village or urban village levels.

Article 23

1. Integrated services for the protection of women and children (PTPPA) at the village or urban village level are carried out by the Village or Urban Village Post. (2) The establishment and facilitation of the operation of the Village or Urban Village Post is the responsibility of the Regional Apparatus Organization in charge of women's empowerment and child protection affairs and the Village Government. (3) The Village or Urban Village Post as referred to in paragraph (1) is established with the tasks: a. providing complaint services; b. providing counseling services; c. providing assistance services; d. providing referral services to the Sub-district and Regency Integrated Service Centers and to other related parties; e. providing social reintegration services f. coordinating case handling; g. collecting data on case handling at the village or urban village level; h. conducting prevention at the village or urban village level. (4) The Integrated Service Center for the protection of women and children (PPTPPA) as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of; a. village or urban village government; b. health clinics and/or village or urban village midwives; c. family empowerment and welfare; d. community organizations; e. religious organizations; f. community-based service institutions; g. women's organizations; and h. religious leaders, community leaders and customary leaders. (5) The structure of the Village or Urban Village Post as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of: a. advisors; b. chairperson; c. secretary; and d. divisions. (6) The structure of the Village or Urban Village Post as referred to in paragraph (1) is established through a decree of the village head or urban village head.

Part Two Principles and Service Standards

Article 19

1. Services to women and children victims of violence as referred to in Article 10 are carried out comprehensively and in an integrated manner across sectors, professions, and disciplines of knowledge.
2. Services as referred to in paragraph (1) are organized with the principles:a. non-discrimination;
b. equality:c. protection and confidentiality;
d. honesty:e. empowerment; andf. integration.
3. Services to women and children victims of violence are carried out based on service standards in accordance with laws and regulations.
4. Service mechanisms for women and children victims of violence are organized according to standard operating procedures.
5. Standard operating procedures as referred to in paragraph (4) are further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 23

1. Integrated services for the protection of women and children (PTPPA) at the village or urban village level are carried out by the Village or Urban Village Post. (2) The establishment and facilitation of the operation of the Village or Urban Village Post is the responsibility of the Regional Apparatus Organization in charge of women's empowerment and child protection affairs and the Village Government. (3) The Village or Urban Village Post as referred to in paragraph (1) is established with the tasks: a. providing complaint services; b. providing counseling services; c. providing assistance services; d. providing referral services to the Sub-district and Regency Integrated Service Centers and to other related parties; e. providing social reintegration services f. coordinating case handling; g. collecting data on case handling at the village or urban village level; h. conducting prevention at the village or urban village level. (4) The Integrated Service Center for the protection of women and children (PPTPPA) as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of; a. village or urban village government; b. health clinics and/or village or urban village midwives; c. family empowerment and welfare; d. community organizations; e. religious organizations; f. community-based service institutions; g. women's organizations; and h. religious leaders, community leaders and customary leaders. (5) The structure of the Village or Urban Village Post as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of: a. advisors; b. chairperson; c. secretary; and d. divisions. (6) The structure of the Village or Urban Village Post as referred to in paragraph (1) is established through a decree of the village head or urban village head.

CHAPTER VII INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS

Article 20

1. Services for women and children victims of violence as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (1) are carried out through an integrated service mechanism.
2. Integrated services as referred to in paragraph (1) are established at the regency, sub-district and village or urban village levels.

CHAPTER VIII COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 24

1. The community and business sector have the right to participate in the prevention of cases of violence against women and children, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence.
2. Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out individually or jointly, either by individuals or institutions.

Article 30

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or Non-Governmental Organizations and Universities that implement protection for women and children victims of violence.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), is in accordance with the regional financial capacity and is implemented in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

3.4.text:
Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Muna Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Muna Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Muna. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Muna Regency. 5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia, can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and includes persons who are legally recognized as Women. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child in the womb. 8. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 9. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life. 10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, serious injury or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death. 12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, sexual abuse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences physical suffering, psychological suffering, sexual suffering, either directly or indirectly resulting from acts of violence. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems they face. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence to family or community who can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs. 22. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their roles normally both in the family and in society. 23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Institution is an agency/service/department/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance. 25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, Safe House, Child Social Protection House, Trauma Center Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter, etc. 26. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and child victims of violence. 27. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and child victims of violence. 28. Safe House is a temporary residence provided to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 29. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion either directly or indirectly based on human differences on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group or class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs resulting from reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 30.

Article 20

1. Services for women and children victims of violence as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (1) are carried out through an integrated service mechanism.

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or Non-Governmental Organizations and Universities that implement protection for women and children victims of violence.

Safe House is a temporary residence provided to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 29. In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Muna Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Muna Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Muna. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Muna Regency. 5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia, can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and includes persons who are legally recognized as Women. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child in the womb. 8. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 9. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life. 10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, serious injury or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death. 12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, sexual abuse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences physical suffering, psychological suffering, sexual suffering, either directly or indirectly resulting from acts of violence. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems they face. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence to family or community who can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs. 22. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their roles normally both in the family and in society. 23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Institution is an agency/service/department/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance. 25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, Safe House, Child Social Protection House, Trauma Center Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter, etc. 26. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and child victims of violence. 27. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and child victims of violence. 28. Safe House is a temporary residence provided to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 29. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion either directly or indirectly based on human differences on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group or class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs resulting from reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 30.

Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia, can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and includes persons who are legally recognized as Women. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child in the womb. 8. Violence is any act against a person that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 9. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life. 10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, serious injury or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death. 12. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, sexual abuse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences physical suffering, psychological suffering, sexual suffering, either directly or indirectly resulting from acts of violence. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems they face. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence to family or community who can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs. 22. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their roles normally both in the family and in society. 23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Institution is an agency/service/department/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance. 25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, Safe House, Child Social Protection House, Trauma Center Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter, etc. 26. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and child victims of violence. 27. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and child victims of violence. 28. Safe House is a temporary residence provided to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 29. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion either directly or indirectly based on human differences on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group or class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs resulting from reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 30.

Article 30

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or Non-Governmental Organizations and Universities that implement protection for women and children victims of violence.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), is in accordance with the regional financial capacity and is implemented in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Article 26

1. Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children is conducted at the end of each fiscal year or when necessary according to needs.
2. The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children are used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children for the following year.
3. Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Article 23

1. Integrated services for the protection of women and children (PTPPA) at the village or urban village level are carried out by the Village or Urban Village Post. (2) The establishment and facilitation of the operation of the Village or Urban Village Post is the responsibility of the Regional Apparatus Organization in charge of women's empowerment and child protection affairs and the Village Government. (3) The Village or Urban Village Post as referred to in paragraph (1) is established with the tasks: a. providing complaint services; b. providing counseling services; c. providing assistance services; d. providing referral services to the Sub-district and Regency Integrated Service Centers and to other related parties; e. providing social reintegration services f. coordinating case handling; g. collecting data on case handling at the village or urban village level; h. conducting prevention at the village or urban village level. (4) The Integrated Service Center for the protection of women and children (PPTPPA) as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of; a. village or urban village government; b. health clinics and/or village or urban village midwives; c. family empowerment and welfare; d. community organizations; e. religious organizations; f. community-based service institutions; g. women's organizations; and h. religious leaders, community leaders and customary leaders. (5) The structure of the Village or Urban Village Post as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of: a. advisors; b. chairperson; c. secretary; and d. divisions. (6) The structure of the Village or Urban Village Post as referred to in paragraph (1) is established through a decree of the village head or urban village head.
